hook: The depth of water at a harbor, the temperature over a day and the hum of a guitar string all rise and fall in smooth, even waves. Before you can write a formula for one, you need four numbers that describe any such wave: how far it swings, where its center line is, how long one cycle takes, and how many cycles fit in one unit of time.

prereq.why: The point on the unit circle returns to the same place after one full turn, $2\pi$.

prereq.q: The graph of $g(x) = f(x) + 3$ is the graph of $f$
options: stretched vertically by a factor of 3
prereq.why: Adding 3 to every output moves each point up 3 units.

figure.caption: For $y = 3\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{4}\right) + 5$: midline $y = 5$, amplitude 3 (midline to maximum), period 8, frequency $\frac{1}{8}$.

chain.cause: Stretch or shrink the graph of sine or cosine and slide it around
chain.effect: you get a sinusoidal function: the same smooth wave shape, with new heights and a new cycle length

chain.cause: Average the greatest and least values
chain.effect: the midline $y = \frac{\max + \min}{2}$, the horizontal line the wave oscillates around

chain.cause: Take half the distance from the least value to the greatest
chain.effect: the amplitude $\frac{\max - \min}{2}$, how far the wave reaches above and below its midline

chain.cause: Measure one full cycle along the input axis
chain.effect: the period $P$; the frequency $\frac{1}{P}$ counts the cycles per unit of input

ideas: A sinusoidal function has the shape of a sine graph after dilations and translations. $y = \sin\theta$ and $y = \cos\theta$ are both sinusoidal, each with amplitude 1, midline $y = 0$ and period $2\pi$.
Amplitude is a distance, so it is never negative. Midline is a line, so write it as an equation: $y = 5$.
Frequency $= \frac{1}{\text{period}}$. A period of 8 seconds means $\frac{1}{8}$ of a cycle per second; 220 cycles per second means a period of $\frac{1}{220}$ second.
Sine is odd, $\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta$; cosine is even, $\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta$.

misconception.wrong: The amplitude is the distance from the lowest point to the highest point.
misconception.right: That distance is twice the amplitude. The amplitude is measured from the midline to the highest point (or to the lowest), so it is half of $\max - \min$.

summary: A sinusoidal function is a sine or cosine graph after dilations and translations. Four numbers describe it: the midline $y = \frac{\max + \min}{2}$, the amplitude $\frac{\max - \min}{2}$, the period (the length of one cycle) and the frequency, one over the period. Sine is odd and cosine is even.
